key_insight: A modular benchmark shows that quantum circuit performance depends on both the search-direction estimator and the classical update rule, and their interaction varies strongly by workload.
engineering_relevance: This framework helps practitioners choose optimizers under finite-shot and hardware constraints by comparing objective progress and sampling cost across QAOA, QML, and VQE tasks.
method: Decouple gradient/derivative-free direction estimation from parameter-update rules.
Benchmark multiple optimizers on QAOA MaxCut, Iris classification, QCNN MNIST, and VQE for H2.
Compare objective values, evaluation counts, classifier accuracy, and finite-shot/hardware behavior.
evidence_signal: The study reports simulator benchmarks over three seeds and four selected simulator/hardware case studies, with terminal and best objectives plus post-training accuracies.
watch_item: The hardware results should not be treated as an optimizer ranking or as evidence of a causal noise effect.
paper_title: Benchmarking Modular Optimization Strategies for Parameterized Quantum Circuits
